experiment_data.hypothesis: The BCS-accuracy correlation in RE arises from semantic confusion rather than forced-choice format artifacts. If removing the enum constraint (relaxed decoding) preserves the negative BCS-accuracy correlation direction and significance, confusability is a genuine semantic property; if the correlation disappears, the effect is specific to constrained classification where all errors are channeled into type substitution. Either outcome strengthens the paper: preservation broadens the claim, disappearance validates the error-channeling hypothesis stated in Discussion.
